commitResults.messageBody:
Document assumptions at task construction, list population, and storage
boundaries using Java assertions. These checks expose programmer errors
early without replacing validation for recoverable user input.
Add assertions for task invariants

Replace abbreviated parameters and local variables with names that
describe their roles. Mark image and application references final so
readers can see that those dependencies do not change after
construction.

Extract focused helpers from the long response dispatcher and name
repeated command prefixes and messages. The flatter control flow and
descriptive constants make each command path easier to understand while
preserving existing behavior.

commitResults.messageTitle: Replace parser magic values with named delimiters
commitResults.messageBody:
Name command prefixes and date delimiters, then derive substring
positions from those constants. Separate malformed-input checks with
guard clauses so the valid parsing path reads clearly and no longer
depends on unexplained offsets.

commitResults.messageTitle: Use stream to serialize task collection
commitResults.messageBody:
Map each task to its stored representation with a Java Stream before
writing the resulting lines. This expresses the collection
transformation directly while preserving the existing file format.
Improve code readability and maintainability
Use streams when saving tasks

Introduce non-completable notes for short reference information while
reusing existing list, find, delete, and storage behavior. Document the
note command and cover parsing, display, persistence, and command
interactions with automated and manual tests.
Add persistent note management

commitResults.messageTitle: Give Trayce a task trail guide personality
commitResults.messageBody:
Introduce a consistent lion-themed voice, greeting, window branding,
and navy-and-gold interface so Trayce has a recognizable personality
across its responses and GUI. Update response tests to cover the new
wording.

Integrate Trayce's task trail guide voice and matching GUI identity
after the feature branch passed the Java 25 test and checkstyle suite.

commitResults.messageTitle: Handle malformed commands and invalid task data
commitResults.messageBody:
Add specific parser errors, date-range and duplicate validation,
task-capacity checks, and resilient storage loading so anticipated user
and environment errors produce useful feedback instead of crashes.
Expand tests to cover each failure path.

Integrate command validation, resilient storage loading, duplicate
prevention, date-range checks, and their Java 25 test coverage.

commitResults.messageTitle: Finalize Trayce product naming and attribution
commitResults.messageBody:
Rename the distributable JAR, replace outdated Duke setup text, improve
Trayce documentation, and credit the course template and JavaFX
resources so the finished product is consistently branded and properly
attributed.

commitResults.messageTitle: Write a complete Trayce user guide
commitResults.messageBody:
Document setup and every supported command with formats, examples,
expected responses, error guidance, and persistence behavior. Add a
real application screenshot and GitHub Pages metadata so users can
learn Trayce from a concise published guide.

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge finalized product guide into master
commitResults.messageBody:
Publish the completed Trayce branding, attribution, executable naming,
and benchmark-aligned user guide with its real GUI screenshot and
GitHub Pages configuration.

commitResults.messageTitle: Add the user guide Pages entry point
commitResults.messageBody:
Render docs/README.md from docs/index.md so GitHub Pages serves the
required Trayce User Guide at the project site root instead of falling
back to the repository README.

commitResults.messageTitle: Place the product screenshot at the required path
commitResults.messageBody:
Move the full-window Trayce screenshot to docs/Ui.png with the exact
required capitalization and update the User Guide image link so both
GitHub Pages and automated checks resolve it correctly.

Trayce has an unused console interface and an older JavaFX interface
in addition to the active FXML application. Keeping multiple entry paths
makes the product structure harder to understand and leaves the console
path with incomplete output behavior.

Remove the obsolete interfaces and console entry point. Document the
active GUI factories and replace raw stack traces with clearer startup
failures.
